ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a benzene ring connected to a nitrogen-containing side chain; hydrogen is attached to the nitrogen, and the side chain continues to a fragment containing C=C and O-H. The figure also shows an isolated H+ and curved arrows. Reasoning: Count only atom connections not involving hydrogen, and ignore arrows. Around the benzene ring there are 6 C-C connections. The bonds in the side chain not involving hydrogen are: aromatic ring C-N, N-C, C-C single bond, C=C, C-O, 5 in total. Ignore N-H, O-H, and isolated H+. The total is 6 + 5 = 11.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible structure, then count only non-H atom connections. Count the six C-C connections around the benzene ring. Add the five non-H bonds in the substituent/side chain: aryl C-N, N-C, C-C single, C=C, and C-O. Ignore N-H, O-H, the isolated H+, and all curved arrows. Sum 6 + 5 = 11.
